document.abstract: The value of the X-rays in the study of medical and surgical problems would be greatly enhanced by the addition of cinematography and, in fact, many medical men impatient with X-ray stills—at best records of single phases only—have begun to ask for new methods of attack along cinematographic lines; in short, for “moving pictures” of the internal organs of the body at work, e. g., the heart beating, the digestive tract dealing with food, and so on.
